comments.body:
**Review of the proof (issue rm-12622-1 was a generic untitled proof task; no specific gap was named, so I performed a full audit).**

**Verdict: the proof is mathematically correct and complete.** It constructs, for any $A:X\to X$ with $F_{A^n}=\{x^*\}$ for all $n\ge1$, an ordinary real metric (the special case $K=\mathbb{R}$, $Q=\lambda\,\mathrm{id}$, $0<\lambda<1$) under which $A$ is a $\lambda$-contraction. This is Bessaga's converse to the Banach contraction principle, validly placed in the $K$-metric framework.

**Audit of each step:**
- *Lemma 1 (no nontrivial periodic points):* direct from $F_{A^k}=\{x^*\}$. Correct.
- *Lemma 2 (orbit dichotomy):* the basin $B$ (orbit reaches $x^*$) vs $X'$ (orbit injective, never $x^*$) is a genuine partition; injectivity in case (b) uses Lemma 1. Correct.
- *Lemma 3 (forward invariance, $N(Az)=N(z)-1$):* correct.
- *$\varphi$ on $B$* via $\lambda^{-N(z)}-1$: gives $\varphi\ge0$, zero iff $z=x^*$, and $\varphi(Az)=\lambda^{-N+1}-1<\lambda^{-N+1}-\lambda=\lambda\varphi(z)$. Correct.
- *$\sim$, $\mathrm{rel}$ on $X'$, and $\varphi=\lambda^{-\mathrm{rel}(x,r_C)}$* (AC for representatives): well-definedness of $\mathrm{rel}$ (Lemma 4) reduces to absence of cycles in $X'$; gives $\varphi(Ax)=\lambda\,\varphi(x)$ exactly. Correct.
- *$K$-metric axioms* for $d(x,y)=\varphi(x)+\varphi(y)$ ($x\ne y$): positivity/faithfulness, symmetry, triangle inequality all check out.
- *Contraction inequality:* follows from $\varphi(Ax)\le\lambda\varphi(x)$ pointwise.

**Numerical verification.** I confirmed $d(Ax,Ay)\le\lambda\,d(x,y)$ in Python on three concrete models satisfying the hypothesis: (i) pure-basin ($X=\mathbb{N}$, $A(n)=\max(n-1,0)$); (ii) pure-$X'$ chain ($A(n)=n+1$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ with $x^*$ adjoined); (iii) a mixed forest (merging basin tree plus a disjoint $X'$ chain). All passed.

**Edit made.** The only weakness was a stylistic ambiguity in Lemma 4 ('say $p<q$'). I rewrote that step symmetrically using $a=\min\{p,q\}$, $b=\max\{p,q\}$, so the cycle-contradiction is manifestly symmetric in $p,q$. No mathematical content changed. (LaTeX compile not run: no toolchain in sandbox.)

solution.tex now stands as a complete and rigorous solution; resolving.
